text:
Dev Patel: can we get a quick runbook snippet for oncall? specifically: given a request id, how do i confirm whether a quant profile was actually applied vs fell back vs disabled

Connor O'Brien: yep, this comes up a lot in beta. rough steps:
1) confirm request id (customer should have `x-redwood-request-id` from response headers; otherwise pull from their app logs if they forward it)
2) check trace/log annotation `quant_profile_id` + `quant_profile_resolution` (applied/fallback/disabled)
3) if fallback, check the reason tag (incompatible / kill-switch / profile_not_found)

Caleb Johnson: tracing path is easiest. in Tempo/Honeycomb (whatever you’re using), search by `request_id` then look for span attrs:
- `route_id`
- `model_id` / `model_variant`
- `quant_profile_id`
- `quant_profile_resolution`
- `quant_profile_fallback_reason` (only present if resolution=fallback)
if attrs missing entirely, you’re probably on an older runtime build or the request never hit the model runtime (blocked upstream).

Noah Patel: +1. runtime started tagging logs + traces with this in the last couple weeks. for logs in Loki, you can do:
``` 
{service="serving-runtime"} |= "request_id=REQ_..." | json | line_format "route={{.route_id}} model={{.model_id}} variant={{.model_variant}} quant={{.quant_profile_id}} res={{.quant_profile_resolution}} reason={{.quant_profile_fallback_reason}}"
```
Expected:
- applied => `quant_profile_id=<profile uuid or named ref>` and `res=applied`
- disabled => `quant_profile_id=none` and `res=disabled`
- fallback => `quant_profile_id=<requested>` and `res=fallback` w/ reason

Ravi Menon: if you need to confirm what the control plane *resolved*, there’s also a policy-engine decision log. search logs for `policy_decision` on that request id. it will show:
- requested ref from route config (`quantization_profile_ref`)
- resolved profile id/version (if any)
- compatibility check result
if policy says “fallback”, runtime should match. if runtime says fallback but policy says applied, escalate to runtime team (possible artifact fetch / load issue).

Chloe Martin: Console also shows current route setting (Route -> Settings -> Quantization). but note Console only shows config “intended state”, not per-request. for per-request verification you need trace/log as folks said.

Aisha Bello: when it’s bigger than a single request (customer says “everything changed”), check dashboards:
- enabled_rate by route
- fallback_rate by route/model/region
- p95 decode latency delta
fallback spikes usually correlate with incompatibility (wrong GPU class) or kill-switch.

Jada Williams: also if the question is “who changed it”, audit log has the route config diffs. search audit events for the route id around the request timestamp. quant settings events include actor + before/after profile ref.

Dev Patel: nice. can we write this as a copy/paste snippet for oncall page? like 6 bullets.

Connor O'Brien: draft snippet:
- Get `x-redwood-request-id` (or internal request id) + approximate timestamp/region
- In tracing, search request id; check span attrs `quant_profile_id` + `quant_profile_resolution` (applied/fallback/disabled)
- If `resolution=fallback`, read `quant_profile_fallback_reason` (common: incompatible_gpu, incompatible_context, kill_switch, profile_fetch_error)
- Cross-check policy decision log (`policy_decision` event) for requested ref + resolved version
- If mismatch policy vs runtime, escalate (#eng-runtime) w/ request id + trace link
- If widespread regression, follow rollback runbook: disable at route level; if still bad, use global kill-switch + page SRE
